correctness.rationale: The exact identifying-code predicate is 16 nonempty distinct closed-ball intersections with a selected 16-bit subset. Fresh independent enumeration of all subsets of cardinality <=7 found none smaller and exactly 960 valid seven-sensor sets. Single replacement of one of 7 selected vertices by one of 9 unselected vertices yields 4320 undirected edges of degree 9. All 960 BFS sources independently yield (1,9,35,132,300,338,130,15) at graph distances 0..7, hence connected radius/diameter 7 and unordered distance counts (4320,16800,63360,144000,162240,62400,7200). Independent generation of all 16*24 Q4 automorphisms gives orbit sizes 192,384,384. This is an exhaustive finite proof on Q4; no higher-dimension statement.

originality.rationale: The known Q4 optimum size seven is expressly prior work. Honkala–Hudry–Lobstein (2015) count optimal identifying codes in constructed graphs, and their paper explicitly points to a separate ensemble paper studying distances between codes: that is substantial conceptual prior overlap. The 2016 ensemble paper describes Johnson-induced ensemble constructions but its full text could not be reached through OA search or authorized institution (VPN disconnected); an actual Q4-specific distance census has not been established from the accessible statements. Resultary semantic query did not return an identical Q4 exchange graph. Best-of-knowledge PASS, carrying a substantial uninspected-primary priority risk.
